column1: # Author: Lane #1644 (Codex). Individual read-based dispositions; repository LF source and final #1693 composition.

column8: The fault fixture fails its selected EdgeRead operation, otherwise executes the complete stored edge read through ReadWithCapability on its supplied stored reader. This is test support, not an independent production fact decoder.

The fault fixture fails its selected NodeRead operation, otherwise delegates complete stored node reading through ReadWithCapability. It retains the injected failure boundary used by public consumer tests.

The transaction edge stream chooses stored visibility on w.tx through VisitWithCapability with no visible fallback, filters namespace before delivery, and projects IDs/endpoints on the issued transaction view.
The issued transaction stored edge point read dispatches on w.tx, prefixes the request once and projects the returned full edge through toUserEdge. No base-store substitution exists.

The issued transaction incoming stored full read dispatches on w.tx with its namespace prefix and projects edges before return; the nil fallback prevents mandatory stored visibility becoming visible reads.
The issued transaction stored node point read dispatches on w.tx, prefixes the request and transforms the full result through toUserNode; native captured/pending semantics remain on that transaction.
The issued transaction outgoing stored full read dispatches on w.tx, retaining the same pending/captured state, then applies its namespace transform.

After the captured full stored scan identifies embedding-bearing IDs, the native point adapter supplies a complete replacement image through the same ReadStored capture/decoder owner. True concurrent absence is recovered before the direct required-error terminal; no hidden-ID disposition is introduced. UpdateNode requires the full labels/properties/hidden image, so metadata-only facts cannot replace this read.

The outgoing-cardinality branch is an existing full physical constraint-graph consumer of native GetStoredOutgoingEdges. It counts matching type/ID after excluding transaction replacements and propagates the stored-read error. This retained full-edge API is not an implementation or claimed cost oracle of metadata-only ReadStored.

The incoming-cardinality branch consumes the corresponding full physical incoming-edge protocol, counts the selected anchor direction and excludes superseded edges. Its native stored owner supplies visibility; no visible-read fallback or independent capture is introduced, and no payload-free cost is claimed for this legacy full-read consumer.

Temporal constraint validation intentionally needs committed temporal/key property values. It streams full stored edges through VisitWithCapability without visible fallback, rejects canceled work, and excludes same-ID, superseded and foreign-namespace records before testing overlap.

Indexed uniqueness candidates request a full stored edge through ReadWithCapability because collides reads constrained property values. Only actual not-found skips the candidate; a hard read or canceled operation terminates validation. This is explicit payload consumption rather than metadata fallback.

The uniqueness scan uses VisitWithCapability to stream full stored edges when no candidate shortcut applies. It filters namespace and transaction supersession before comparing constrained properties and propagates callback/refusal errors without replay or visible fallback.

Label-policy revalidation is an existing full constraint-graph outgoing-edge consumer. It replaces committed edges with pending mutations, skips deletions/foreign records and uses the retained node-label owner for endpoint policy checks. It does not implement the mandatory metadata-only operation or promise excluded-payload cost.

The incoming label-policy pass uses the native full stored adjacency owner, then orients the changed node as the target when comparing endpoint labels. Pending/deleted-edge handling stays with the transaction; stored-read errors terminate validation rather than producing an empty successful policy check.

Idempotent hidden-edge CREATE commit validation requires the predecessor's full identity/properties to compare with the staged candidate. It uses the native stored point owner and returns an error for a missing, unreadable or newly visible predecessor; it does not use visible matching to accept the no-op.

The transaction's full stored label collection is a thin collector over its own StreamStoredNodesByLabelProjected. That stream retains the captured transaction and overlay with stored visibility; the collector returns its terminal error with the requested full nodes.

storedEdgeEndpoints already has one fact-only ReadStoredMetadata branch. Its remaining full GetStoredEdge is used only when a caller explicitly requests image **Edge for later replacement/history; removing that body would change the requested output.

The native constraint-graph incoming-edge owner requires full Edge values for its public constraintGraphView protocol. It reads stored committed edges through the native captured reader, then merges pending replacements and deletions before schema validators consume them. This is an intentional full graph/image interface, not a metadata substitute.

The native constraint-graph outgoing-edge owner reads the full stored adjacency through its existing capture owner and overlays pending/deleted edges. Its callers are transaction/publication constraint views, which retain a full-image protocol; it does not create another synchronized capture implementation.
The scoped stored label full-read adapter first dispatches contextually, then uses the same-view stored legacy operation with no visible fallback. Scope and label remain explicit request inputs.

The contextual stored-label facade first binds an exact contextual capability, then a StoredEntityReader operation on the same issued view. Its ordinary fallback belongs only to the existing full-read compatibility API; mandatory ReadStored never consumes that weaker fallback.

The scoped stored projected stream keeps scope, selected properties and context across the common visit protocol; legacy dispatch is nested through the same owner and cannot replay after delivered rows.
The stored projected label stream uses VisitWithCapability for both contextual and legacy providers, preserving requested projection and no-delivery refusal semantics.

After VisitWithCapability selects the actual stored provider, arbitrary unscoped snapshot readers retain StreamStoredEdgesByType and their interception. The selected writer sends each frame through deliver, so a late refusal cannot replay already-written output on a native child.

The WAL full projected-label method delegates once to its scoped operation with empty scope. That method uses the shared stored capability cursor on w.engine, preserving the requested projection and visitor error; no private unwrap or whole-graph fallback is added.

The full stored edge compatibility facade selects StoredEntityReader through ReadWithCapability and returns its point error. Its same-issued-view GetEdge fallback is the release full-read contract only; stronger mandatory stored metadata remains a separate refusal-capable request to the same execution owner.
Incoming full stored read selects context support exactly on the chosen stored reader; legacy and ordinary alternatives remain within the common same-view operation, with cancellation returned.
The legacy full node helper keeps the complete-image contract through ReadWithCapability and a documented same-original-Engine ordinary alternative; it is not the stored-presence owner.

The full stored label compatibility facade binds the StoredEntityReader operation and same-view ordinary label fallback through ReadWithCapability. It never serves as mandatory physical metadata or claims payload exclusion; callback/error selection stays with the common operation owner.
Outgoing full stored read adapts context exactly on the selected stored reader, then uses the common same-view legacy/ordinary alternatives; no bare physical unwrap occurs.
Full stored edge streaming uses VisitWithCapability and the original Engine's ordinary edge stream when its legacy contract permits absence fallback; delivery ownership prevents replay after rows.
Scoped full edge streaming first selects ScopedStoredEntityReader under the common visit protocol; scope and type remain attached to that operation.

If scoped support refuses before delivery, the legacy stored reader is selected through a nested common visit operation, retaining the original outer operation's delivery guard before ordinary scope fallback.
